answer.because: The script runs the real `npm pack` on the tree, unpacks the tarball as node_modules/semver, then requires `semver` and, if the tree has a preload.js, `semver/preload`; on head the packed file list has no preload.js and `require('semver/preload')` throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND, so the 'files' allowlist leaves the new module out of the published package, while on base `semver` loads and there is no preload.js to check.
